To Whom It May Concern,

Our patient may return to work on light duty with the following restrictions:

• No lifting, pushing, or pulling greater than 12 pounds  
• Remote work is recommended when possible  
• Restrictions are contingent upon the patient’s pain levels, medication use, and ongoing recovery status pending upcoming MRI imaging and follow-up evaluation in June 2026  

If the patient is experiencing increased pain requiring heavy pain medication, she should not operate a vehicle and should remain remote/off-site if possible until symptoms improve.

At this time, a definitive end date for restrictions cannot yet be determined, as recovery and work capacity remain dependent on clinical progress and upcoming diagnostic review.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Sincerely,  
[Provider Name / Practice Name]

Here’s a more polished and professional version that still sounds human and apologetic:

:::writing{variant="email" id="48271" subject="Updated Work Restrictions"}
I apologize for the delay in getting this over to you. I had to follow up with the surgeon’s office multiple times by phone and email before they were able to provide the documentation.

My surgeon is taking a conservative approach with my recovery, but I explained that I do need to begin resuming work responsibilities in some capacity. Based on that conversation, he agreed to allow me to return with restrictions in place.

With that said, I would like to resume coming into the office on Mondays and begin handling the mail again. If at any point I am unable to drive due to pain or medication, I will communicate that as soon as possible.

Thank you again for your patience and understanding.
:::
